methodological_rigor.justification: The study applies a rigorous, multi-layered experimental design spanning biophysical SPR/koff measurements, in vitro Jurkat reporter and primary T-cell assays, xenograft and humanized NSG-SGM3 CRS mouse models, and single-cell RNA sequencing, with orthogonal validation on ROR1 CARs. Key controls are appropriate (mock-transduced T cells, CD19-negative targets, PMA/ionomycin positive controls, dose matching for affinity-combined products), and donor variability is addressed through biological replicates from multiple healthy donors and parallel mouse experiments. Sample sizes per mouse cohort are modest (n = 4 to 8) and biological replicate counts vary across panels (n = 3 to 7), with no formal power calculation reported. Statistics use one-way/two-way ANOVA, log-rank for survival, and Mann-Whitney U for scRNA-seq differential expression, with p-value thresholds and multiple-comparisons-to-reference specified, though explicit multiplicity correction across dimensions and effect sizes/CIs beyond mean ± SD are not consistently reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work has direct translational relevance to CAR-T therapy design because it identifies an implementable strategy (affinity-combined CAR-T products) that could reduce CRS severity and exhaustion while preserving anti-tumor efficacy, issues central to currently approved CD19 CAR-T products. The use of clinically relevant scFvs (FMC63-derived JCAR017 and humanized JCAR021) and validation in a humanized CRS model strengthens clinical applicability. However, all evidence is preclinical (in vitro and xenograft/humanized mice), with no human data, so the Oxford level of evidence maps to 5 (preclinical/mechanistic). Near-term clinical development appears plausible given that both CARs are already used in clinical-stage products, but feasibility of co-formulation and optimal ratio remain to be established.

reporting_quality.justification: As a preclinical study with extensive animal work, ARRIVE is the applicable standard; the manuscript reports mouse strain, housing conditions, age/sex, randomization implied by donor-matched experiments, ethics approvals (district government of Upper Bavaria ROB-55.2-2532.Vet_02-18-162), humane endpoints, and group sizes per figure legend, indicating thorough adherence with minor omissions (no explicit blinding statement, no a priori sample-size calculation). The Methods are detailed and reproducible, covering vector construction, SPR, koff assay, scRNA-seq pipeline (SCANPY v1.9.1, CellRanger 7.0.0, GRCh38-2024-A), and cytokine assays. A 'Source data' section and 'Reporting Summary' are referenced, suggesting some data availability, but no explicit data repository accession or code repository is identified in the provided text, limiting full reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: The central concept of combining high- and low-affinity CARs targeting the same epitope within a single product to simultaneously mitigate CRS/exhaustion and preserve efficacy is a genuinely novel strategic framing that extends beyond prior affinity-tuning work (e.g., Ghorashian 2019, Olson 2022, He 2023, Barden 2024 cited). The authors also generate an unprecedentedly broad affinity library of 32 JCAR021 mutants spanning down to TCR-like koff-rates and apply a TCR-avidity-derived flow cytometry koff assay to CARs, which is methodologically original. The scRNA-seq analysis showing that high-affinity CAR-T transcriptional state is modulated by co-administered low-affinity CAR-T cells is a meaningful mechanistic advance. It is an incremental extension rather than a paradigm shift because affinity tuning per se is well-established and the mechanism (competitive antigen engagement) is only speculated.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with a logical progression from biophysical characterization through in vitro, in vivo toxicity, combination in vitro, and combination in vivo with scRNA-seq. Figure legends are detailed with n-values, statistical tests, and panel-specific descriptions. The abstract, introduction, and discussion effectively contextualize findings against prior literature. Some sentences are dense and occasional minor issues appear (e.g., a stray double-period in the Fig. 6 title 'administered with low-affinity CARs..'), and figure-panel letter k is referenced in Fig. 4 where j is expected, but these are minor. Overall, presentation is publication-quality.

key_strengths: Novel affinity-combination CAR-T concept validated with orthogonal CD19 and ROR1 systems, not just a single target
Unusually broad affinity spectrum (32 JCAR021 mutants down to TCR-like koff-rates) enabled by an adapted flow-cytometry koff assay
Use of humanized NSG-SGM3 CRS model with rederived single-donor cohorts provides clinically meaningful toxicity readouts
Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies reduced exhaustion signatures (CCL5, TOX) and enhanced cytotoxic program in high-affinity CAR-T cells when co-administered with low-affinity CARs
Thorough experimental controls including dose-matched and half-dose JCAR017 conditions to rule out simple dose-dilution effects
key_concerns: All data are preclinical; no patient samples or clinical correlates, and optimal affinity ratio is acknowledged as undetermined
Mechanism of the synergistic effect is speculative (competitive antigen engagement) and not directly tested
Modest mouse cohort sizes (n = 4 to 8) with no a priori power calculation and limited explicit multiplicity correction
Findings largely restricted to CD19/4-1BB context with only proof-of-principle ROR1 extension; CD28-based CARs not tested
Data availability limited to a Source Data reference without explicit repository accession or code repository citation in the provided text
chief_reviewer.rationale: The manuscript presents a methodologically solid, mechanistically informative, and translationally relevant preclinical study with clear novelty in the affinity-combination framing and in the breadth of the affinity library, appropriate for a Tier 2 journal (e.g., Nature Communications oncology scope or Clinical Cancer Research); lack of clinical data and unresolved mechanism preclude Tier 1.
